security.metaTitle: Free Antivirus for Mac, Powered by ClamAV · OpenNavo
security.description: Free, open-source malware scanning for Mac with ClamAV. Checks installers before they install, new downloads, startup items and app signatures.

hero.title: Free, open-source antivirus for Mac,
hero.lede: OpenNavo scans your Mac with the **ClamAV** engine and its official database, then adds **pre-install scans**, download checks, startup item reviews and signature check-ups. Everything runs on your Mac: no uploads, no account.

layers.title: Six checks, each with its own job.
layers.body: The virus database recognizes known malicious files. Signature, notarization and startup item checks cover what a database can’t see.

scan.title: The usual hiding spots in minutes, or the whole Mac.
scan.body: The engine uses about 1.1 GB of memory while scanning and quits after 5 idle minutes. Threats can be quarantined, deleted or trusted, and anything in quarantine can be restored.

quick.title: Quick Scan
quick.body: Programs that startup items run, Downloads, Desktop, temporary folders and apps installed in the last 7 days

full.title: Full Scan
full.body: The whole Mac, except the system volume, iCloud files not downloaded, Time Machine and network volumes

custom.title: Custom Scan
custom.body: Choose folders or an external drive

schedule.title: Scheduled scans
schedule.body: A quick scan at the time you set. It runs only while OpenNavo is open, skips when on battery and never wakes your Mac

startup.title: Everything that starts on its own, in one list.
startup.body: Twenty kinds of startup items, grouped by app, with signature, notarization and owner shown. New items trigger an alert right away, and anything you disable or remove can be restored.

points.trust: Apple, known developers and unsigned programs are told apart, so suspicious items stand out
points.alerts: An alert the moment a new startup item, login item or background service appears
points.restore: Items are backed up before they’re disabled or removed, so you can always restore them

startup.categoriesTitle: The 20 kinds of startup items it checks

posture.title: Is macOS’s own protection switched on?
posture.body: A read-only check of 11 system settings that changes nothing. When something needs fixing, OpenNavo opens the right pane in System Settings.

extras.title: Off by default, there when you want them.

paste.title: Paste protection
paste.body: When you press ⌘V to paste a suspicious “download and run” command into a terminal, OpenNavo pauses and asks first. The check runs locally, and nothing you paste is stored.

virusTotal.title: VirusTotal lookup
virusTotal.body: Look up a file’s SHA-256 on VirusTotal with your own API key. Only the hash is sent; the file never leaves your Mac.

pasteDemo.title: Paste into “Terminal” paused
pasteDemo.body: This command looks like it downloads and runs a program. Discard it unless you meant to run it.

vtDemo.hashOnly: Only the file’s SHA-256 was sent; the file wasn’t uploaded

privacy.title: Your files stay on your Mac.

local.title: Scanned locally
local.body: Scans run on your Mac, and results are stored only there.

database.title: Official database
database.body: The database comes straight from ClamAV’s official servers, not through OpenNavo.

hashes.title: No uploads
hashes.body: The optional VirusTotal lookup sends only a file’s SHA-256, and only if you turn it on.

need.a: macOS ships with Gatekeeper, notarization and XProtect, which stop many known threats. Cracked software, installers from unknown sites and commands pasted into Terminal are still common ways in. OpenNavo adds a check at each of those points. It complements the protection in macOS rather than replacing it.

database.q: Where does the virus database come from, and how often is it updated?
database.a: It’s ClamAV’s official database, downloaded straight from ClamAV’s servers rather than through OpenNavo. The first download is about 113 MB (about 170 MB on disk). After that, OpenNavo checks every 4 hours by default and downloads only the changes.

performance.q: Will it slow my Mac down?
performance.a: The engine uses about 1.1 GB of memory while scanning and quits after 5 idle minutes, so it uses nothing the rest of the time. Scheduled scans run only while OpenNavo is open, skip when on battery and never wake your Mac.

upload.a: No. Scans run on your Mac and results stay there. The optional VirusTotal lookup has to be turned on with your own API key, and even then it sends only the file’s SHA-256.

realtime.q: Does it block malware in real time?
realtime.a: New downloads and new startup items are checked as soon as they appear, and you’re alerted right away, but OpenNavo can’t yet stop a program before its first run. Real-time blocking needs Apple’s Endpoint Security entitlement and will come once it’s granted.

coverage.q: Will it catch every piece of Mac malware?
coverage.a: No antivirus can promise that. ClamAV’s coverage of Mac-specific malware is limited, which is why OpenNavo also checks signatures, notarization and startup items, and shows the status of XProtect. Ordinary files over 100 MB, and installers over 1 GB or over 2 GB once unpacked, aren’t fully scanned.

price.a: Yes, and it needs no account. OpenNavo is open source under GPL-3.0, with its code on GitHub.

cta.title: Give your Mac one more check.
cta.body: OpenNavo is free, open source and runs on macOS 13 or later. The first time you scan, it asks before downloading the official database.

security.title: Scanned before it installs. Watched after.
security.body: OpenNavo ships the open-source **ClamAV** engine, with its database updated straight from ClamAV’s official servers. Apps you install through OpenNavo are scanned before they install, and new downloads and new startup items are checked as soon as they appear. Scans run on your Mac, and **no files are uploaded**.

scan.title: Quick, full and scheduled scans
scan.body: A quick scan checks Downloads, the Desktop and startup items in minutes and can run every day or week. A full scan covers the whole Mac.

install.title: Scanned before install
install.body: After Homebrew downloads an app and before it installs, the download is scanned. A threat stops the install.

downloads.title: New downloads, checked
downloads.body: OpenNavo watches your Downloads folder and scans each file when it finishes. Installers also get a signature and notarization check.

startup.title: Startup items
startup.body: Twenty kinds, from background services and login items to browser extensions, each with its signature and owning app. New ones trigger an alert right away.

signatures.title: Signature check-up
signatures.body: Checks the signature and notarization of every installed app, and warns you when an app’s developer signature suddenly changes, a sign it may have been replaced.

posture.title: System check-up
posture.body: SIP, Gatekeeper, FileVault, the firewall, XProtect and six more settings, so you can see at a glance what’s switched off.

security.note: ClamAV’s coverage of Mac-specific malware is limited, so OpenNavo also checks signatures, notarization and startup items. It adds to the protection built into macOS; it doesn’t replace it.

catalog.body: Install, update and uninstall, all in one place. Rankings follow **real installs from the last 30 days**, and **editor’s picks** and **collections** help you find the good ones.

homebrew.title: The Homebrew catalog
homebrew.body: Synced daily from Homebrew’s official catalog. Homebrew does the installing and updating, and you can see every command and log line.

appStore.title: Mac App Store apps
appStore.body: Search App Store apps right in the app, with details straight from Apple. Sign in with your Apple Account to install and update them.

link.title: Developer downloads
link.body: Apps that aren’t in Homebrew link to the developer’s official download. OpenNavo doesn’t host installers, and it checks the signature once a download finishes.

details.title: Every version, on the record.
details.body: When Homebrew picks up a new version, it shows up here with the exact commit time. The **release notes** we write are translated into your language automatically, with the original one click away.

points.about: Descriptions, screenshots, and install details before you install
points.deps: Dependencies, conflicts, and install locations at a glance
points.languages: Six languages, falling back to English or the original when a translation is missing

install.title: One click, installed.
install.body: Click Get on an app page and OpenNavo runs Homebrew on your Mac to install it. You can see **the exact command** and **every line of the log**. When administrator rights are needed, macOS asks for your password, and OpenNavo never stores it.

points.queue: Tasks run in a queue, can be canceled, and can be retried if they fail
points.scan: Downloads are scanned for malware before they install; a threat stops the install
points.history: Every install, update, and removal is recorded on your Mac

updates.title: Updates, handled.
updates.body: A daily check gathers updates from Homebrew, the App Store, Sparkle, Electron and GitHub, with the count in the **menu bar**. One click on **Update All** takes care of the rest.

points.schedule: Daily checks at a set time, with optional notifications
points.verify: Updates from outside Homebrew must carry the same developer signature, or they aren’t installed
points.rollback: Apps that support it roll back to the previous version in one click
points.pin: Pin an app or skip a version, and Update All leaves it alone

toolkit.title: It looks after your Mac, too.
toolkit.body: Uninstall apps along with their leftovers, see what a cleanup will free before it runs, and keep CPU, memory, temperatures and fans in your menu bar.

uninstall.title: Uninstall without leftovers
uninstall.body: Uninstall apps from Homebrew, the App Store or a developer’s site. Their data, caches, preferences and background items are found too, and files shared with other apps stay by default.

cleanup.title: Look first, then clean
cleanup.body: A read-only scan takes about 30 seconds and sorts what it finds into three risk tiers. Caches are deleted; leftovers go to the Trash, where you can undo. Keychains, VPNs and virtual machines are always protected.

monitor.title: Monitoring in the menu bar
monitor.body: CPU, GPU, memory, disk, network, battery, temperatures and fans: put any of them in the menu bar, and set fan speeds too.

handoff.title: Find on the web, install in the app
handoff.body: Click Open in OpenNavo on the web. The app shows the command it will run and installs only after you confirm.

mirrors.title: Mirror speed test
mirrors.body: OpenNavo tests the official source and the mirrors, then recommends the fastest. Homebrew setup and brew commands use it, and you can switch at any time.

brewfile.title: New Mac, same apps
brewfile.body: Add your apps to a list and export a Brewfile. On a new Mac, one command installs them all.

search.title: Search with ⌘K
search.body: Search by English name, Chinese name, pinyin, or common aliases. Typing vscode finds Visual Studio Code.

languages.title: Six languages
languages.body: The interface speaks English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, Portuguese, and Russian, with dates and numbers to match.

privacy.title: No account needed
privacy.body: No sign-in, and we don’t collect which apps you have installed. Malware scans run on your Mac, and your Brewfile list stays in your browser.

cta.title: Start with your next app.
cta.body: OpenNavo is free and open source, with malware scanning, cleanup and monitoring included. It runs on macOS 13 or later. You can also browse on the web and copy the brew command to install.
